subject: SIG: Incident disclosure window, POC handoffs, and escalation fallbacks
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@greenbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: SIG: Clarify breach disclosure windows and POC roster

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the SIG questions — a couple items came up during our procurement review that we need clarified before we proceed to the next security review. Short bullets below: 

- Notification window: GreenBank requires confirmation of whether Redwood follows a 72-hour disclosure window for confirmed incidents affecting customer data (we classify as regulated PII). If you have tiers (e.g., 4-hour ack, 72-hour disclosure), please spell them out.
- POC & escalation roster: We require explicit POC names and a fallback escalation roster per region (US/EU). Can you provide names, titles, and a 24/7 fallback plan?
- Evidence submission: preferred secure channels for submitting evidence (SFTP/ShareFile/portal) and expected turnaround for providing SOC 2 artifacts or redacted logs once a request is validated.
- Auditability: will Redwood provide a timeline for public disclosure and customer notification responsibility (do you notify impacted customers or provide notice templates to customers)?

We'd like these clarified in writing; a short recorded 30-min runthrough is fine if useful. Please also indicate any non-disclosure constraints around sharing SOC 2 artifacts.

Attached is our SIG worksheet excerpt (GreenBank_SIG_Questions.xlsx) with the specific rows we flagged.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Monday 22 Jun if possible.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Senior InfoSec Analyst
GreenBank

Soojin — answering inline and attaching the artifacts you requested. I've redacted internal-runbook links and customer identifiers. Attachments: IR_Playbook_excerpt.pdf (redacted), contact_matrix_v2.csv.

Summary answers:
- Timelines (high-level): initial inbound triage ack: within 4 hours (business hours) or within 1 hour outside business hours if triggered by monitoring alert; formal incident classification & internal triage completed within 24 hours; customer-notification window for confirmed incidents that materially affect customer data: standard is 72 hours from classification/confirmation (this aligns to what GreenBank noted). For incidents that require regulator notification sooner we escalate to legal and may shorten timelines accordingly.
- POC & escalation roster: primary POC per region (US/EU) + two named fallbacks. For GreenBank specifically we propose: Soojin Lee (Security Program Manager, primary), Karthik Iyer (Director, Security Ops, escalation 1), Mina Haddad (Head of Trust, escalation 2). If primary is unreachable >2 hours, escalation goes to the next named person; if all named are unavailable, the on-call responder (rotating ops lead) is engaged. Contact matrix attached includes mobile, pager, and after-hours escalation steps.
- Evidence transfer: preferred channels we support are (1) encrypted SFTP with pre-shared keys, (2) secure ShareFile link with tenant-restricted upload, or (3) a temporary secure portal session (we can set up per-request). We do not accept HTTP attachments over email. Typical turnaround: redacted SOC2 artifacts and attestation letter within 3 business days after NDA/validated request; deeper log exports requiring engineering time will have ETA in the initial 24-hour triage note.
- Customer notification responsibility: Redwood will provide the affected-customer list (if the incident is customer-scoped) and a notification template. We can either (A) issue a customer notification on behalf of customers (rare, requires contract language) or (B) provide a template and the data needed for the customer to send. Default: we supply the template + evidence package and recommend customers send notices themselves unless contractually requested otherwise.

Notes: Attached is the redacted IR playbook excerpt (PDF) and a contact matrix CSV. Also attached SOC2 attestation letter for 2025 — this is the standard certified attestation; further workpapers require NDAs.

I'll leave the external phrasing to you / Marissa — suggest keeping the reply concise and offering a 30-min call to walk GreenBank's InfoSec through the attachments.

Karthik
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear questions. Attached are three redacted items we can share immediately: a short excerpt from our IR playbook (redacted for customer IDs), a contact matrix with primary and fallback POCs for US/EU, and our SOC2 Attestation Letter (2025).

High-level takeaways for GreenBank: 
- Acknowledgement SLA: initial triage acknowledgement within 4 hours (1 hour for critical monitoring alerts outside business hours).
- Customer disclosure: standard window for confirmed incidents materially affecting customer data is 72 hours from confirmation/classification (we escalate to legal for regulator-driven timelines).
- POCs & fallbacks: primary POC for US incidents is me (Soojin Lee); escalation path is Karthik Iyer then Mina Haddad. The attached contact matrix includes after-hours pager and fallback instructions.
- Evidence transfer: we prefer encrypted SFTP or tenant-restricted ShareFile. We can accept a secure upload once an NDA/validation is completed. SOC2 attestation and redacted evidence can be provided within ~3 business days after validation; detailed logs may take longer depending on scope and engineering involvement.
- Notification approach: by default we provide templates and the evidence package; if you require Redwood to send notifications on behalf of customers, that needs contractual approval.

If useful, I'd like to set a 30-minute call to walk through the playbook excerpt and the contact matrix. Marissa — can you please propose 2 slots?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Program Manager
